kept.q: Who was the mother of Samuel, who dedicated her son to serve God at the tabernacle in Shiloh after he was weaned?
kept.explanation: Hannah prayed for a son and promised to give him to God's service. When Samuel was born, she kept her vow and took him to Shiloh. This is recorded in 1 Samuel 1:20-28.
kept.pidgin: Na Hannah pray God make im get pikin, im promise say im go give the pikin to God service. When Samuel born, Hannah carry am go Shiloh as im promise. Dis dey for 1 Samuel 1:20-28.

kept.q: Under whose care did the young Samuel grow up and serve while ministering at the tabernacle in Shiloh?
kept.explanation: Hannah left Samuel with Eli the priest at Shiloh, where the boy grew up serving before the Lord. God later called Samuel while he was under Eli's care. See 1 Samuel 3:1.
kept.pidgin: Hannah leave Samuel with Eli the priest for Shiloh, na so the boy dey grow dey serve God. Na there God call Samuel first time. E dey for 1 Samuel 3:1.

kept.q: According to 1 Samuel chapter 15, what exact disobedience caused God to reject Saul as king of Israel?
options: He failed to completely destroy the Amalekites and their livestock as commanded
He refused to go to war against the Philistines
He married a woman from a forbidden nation
He built an altar to a foreign god on Mount Carmel
kept.explanation: God commanded Saul to destroy the Amalekites and all their animals completely, but Saul spared King Agag and the best animals. Samuel told him that obedience is better than sacrifice. This is in 1 Samuel 15:3, 9, 22-23.
kept.pidgin: God tell Saul make im destroy all Amalekite people and their animals finish, but Saul leave King Agag and the best animals. Samuel talk say to obey pass sacrifice. E dey for 1 Samuel 15:3, 9, 22-23.

kept.q: Who anointed David as king over Israel while his brothers stood watching at Jesse's house in Bethlehem?
kept.explanation: God sent Samuel to Jesse's house to anoint one of his sons as king. After rejecting the older sons, Samuel anointed David, the youngest, as the Spirit of the Lord came upon him. This is in 1 Samuel 16:1-13.
kept.pidgin: God send Samuel go Jesse house make im anoint one of im sons as king. Afta e reject the big brothers, Samuel anoint David wey be the last born, and Spirit of God come enter am. E dey for 1 Samuel 16:1-13.

kept.q: What weapon did David use to defeat the Philistine giant Goliath on the battlefield at the Valley of Elah?
options: A sling and a smooth stone
kept.explanation: David refused Saul's armour and instead chose five smooth stones and his sling, striking Goliath on the forehead with one stone. He then used Goliath's own sword to kill him. This is recorded in 1 Samuel 17:40, 49-50.
kept.pidgin: David no gree wear Saul armour, im pick five smooth stones with im sling, im hit Goliath for forehead with one stone. Na Goliath im sword im later use finish am. E dey for 1 Samuel 17:40, 49-50.

kept.q: Why did King Saul become jealous and afraid of David after his victory over Goliath and the Philistines?
options: The women of Israel sang that David had killed tens of thousands while Saul had killed only thousands
David married Saul's daughter without asking permission
David refused to serve as a soldier in Saul's army
Saul's own son Jonathan crowned David king in public
kept.explanation: When the army returned from battle, women sang that Saul had slain thousands but David had slain ten thousands. This song made Saul jealous and suspicious of David from that day. See 1 Samuel 18:6-9.
kept.pidgin: When soldiers dey comot from war, women sing say Saul kill thousand but David kill ten thousand. Dis song make Saul jealous and im begin suspect David from that day. E dey for 1 Samuel 18:6-9.

kept.q: When Samuel looked at Jesse's eldest son Eliab and was impressed by his height and appearance, what lesson did God teach him before David was chosen as king?
options: That God chooses leaders mainly by their outward appearance and height
That the first son of any family always inherits leadership
That God looks at the heart, not outward appearance, when choosing a leader
That physical strength is the most important quality for a king
kept.explanation: Samuel assumed Eliab's impressive looks meant he was God's choice, but God told him not to judge by outward appearance because man looks at the outside while God looks at the heart. This teaching came just before David was anointed. See 1 Samuel 16:6-7.
kept.pidgin: Samuel think say Eliab fine body mean say na im be the choice, but God tell am make im no judge by outside appearance because man dey see outside, God dey see inside heart. Na so e be before David anointing. E dey for 1 Samuel 16:6-7.

kept.q: Who was Saul's father, a man of standing from the tribe of Benjamin, as recorded in 1 Samuel?
kept.explanation: Saul was the son of Kish, a wealthy and respected man of the tribe of Benjamin. Saul was sent to search for his father's lost donkeys when he first met Samuel. This is in 1 Samuel 9:1-3.
kept.pidgin: Saul na son of Kish, wey be rich and respected man from Benjamin tribe. Na when Saul dey find im papa donkeys wey lost, e first meet Samuel. E dey for 1 Samuel 9:1-3.
